finding: Rewriting BETWEEN into two comparisons duplicates the left operand; two controlled quota counterexamples involve LOWER and LENGTH. A generic three-argument scalar fix would eagerly evaluate upper bounds and alter SQLite WHERE short-circuiting.
scope: Only syntactically proven length(...) with signed i64/NULL literal bounds retains SQLite native INTEGER/NULL BETWEEN. Original literal AST nodes are walked for limits and each proven integer replaces its existing parameter slot with I64, preserving SQL placeholder order. Other expressions keep previous rewrite.

boundaries: Nine distinct final targeted tests, not full SQL, HostLab/A0/A1, Linux, formal performance or profile qualification. LOWER and other complex operands still have duplicated evaluation. Input nodes are checked before integer normalization; normal SQL/SQLite buffers and RSS remain outside this proof.
